I don't have any notes on Isaiah 17 for you yet. My one attempt to fetch the sources failed, and the tool won't let me make any more calls in this turn.

I tried to fetch six pages at once:
- Enduring Word on Isaiah 17 (enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-17/)
- Ellicott's commentary on Isaiah 17 (biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/isaiah/17.htm)
- Gill's commentary on Isaiah 17 (biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/17.htm)
- Pulpit Commentary on Isaiah 17 (biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/isaiah/17.htm)
- GotQuestions on Damascus in prophecy (gotquestions.org/Damascus-in-prophecy.html)
- NET Bible notes on Isaiah 17 (netbible.org/bible/Isaiah+17)

A bug in my code meant I never read what came back, so I can't say whether any of the pages loaded. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, since they would have come from memory rather than the sources.

If you ask me to try again, I'll:
1. Read those six pages properly and write the traditional reading verse by verse (v. 1–14), with a URL for each point.
2. Look for where Protestant traditions really differ. Likely places are vv. 7–8 (people turning to their Maker: real repentance or not?) and vv. 12–14 (usually tied to Assyria's army destroyed overnight in Isaiah 37:36). I'd search desiringgod.org, gty.org, ligonier.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's Notes), lcms.org and ccel.org (for example Calvin's and Matthew Henry's commentaries).
3. Cover other views: NET Bible notes and bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship, and newadvent.org or catholic.com for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'd also cover the popular claim that verse 1 is a future end-times destruction of Damascus, as the sites describe it, and say which ones accept or reject it.
